sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup
sections.what: Loads the file system and hashing tools and states what the script does.
sections.why: Gives a clear statement of purpose at the top of the file.

sections.name: sha
sections.title: Fingerprint helper and download time
sections.what: Defines a helper that fingerprints a file, reads when the data was downloaded, and creates the fixture folder.
sections.why: Fingerprints show a file is unchanged.
sections.watch_out: The helper reads the whole file into memory to fingerprint it, which is slow for large files.

sections.name: openf1Files
sections.title: Copy OpenF1 and StatsBomb samples
sections.what: Copies the OpenF1 race files that exist, then copies the StatsBomb files, compressing the event files.
sections.why: Small samples are kept in the repo so tests have data to use.
sections.watch_out: A file missing from the raw folder is skipped without error, so tests may pass with less data.

sections.name: sources
sections.title: Source list
sections.what: Builds the list of sources with each one's web address, local file, attribution, size, fingerprint and download time, including the Cricsheet record.
sections.why: Attribution must travel with the data.
sections.watch_out: StatsBomb web addresses are rebuilt from file names, so a renamed file gives a wrong address.

sections.name: outputs
sections.title: Output list and manifest
sections.what: Fingerprints every output file in the fixture and derived folders, lists any missing items, and writes the manifest.
sections.watch_out: The run fails if any listed folder does not exist.

summary: Copies the small sample data into the fixtures folder and writes a manifest recording where each file came from and its fingerprint.
purpose: Keeps a record of sources, download times, fingerprints and attribution, so the data can be trusted and credited.
why: The file header states this purpose; fingerprints let anyone check that files have not changed.
how: Copies the OpenF1 files, compresses the StatsBomb event files and copies the rest, then gathers source details from the download records, computes SHA-256 fingerprints, lists the output files and writes data/manifest.json.
inputs: Raw data folders, a download time file, and the Cricsheet fetch record.
outputs: Copies in data/fixtures, data/manifest.json, and a printed summary line.
risks: Missing folders stop the run. Missing optional files are skipped silently, so the manifest may not list everything expected.
debug: Open data/manifest.json and check which sources and missing items it lists.
